title: Diversity Prediction Theorem as a Safety Audit for Multi-Model Aggregation

original_idea.body:
# Diversity Prediction Theorem as a Safety Audit

On numeric-estimate safety tasks with ground truth, run a model panel and empirically decompose collective squared error into average-individual-error and predictive-diversity components, showing how much crowd benefit homogeneity has eaten. Inference + arithmetic decomposition.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — quantifies how homogeneity undermines aggregation-based safety via a single interpretable decomposition.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: numeric-estimate tasks + a simple decomposition formula; ideal for a stats background.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped error decomposition with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public models + labeled tasks, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Empirical DPT decomposition for LLM safety panels appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: No known empirical DPT decomposition for LLM safety aggregation.
